facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 8:00 AM ET

The 2026 Formula 1 season is heading to a dramatic finale.

Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos last weekend, posting a 10-second victory margin that showed McLaren's race pace is as formidable as ever. The win extended the championship battle and ensured the title fight will not be resolved before Las Vegas on November 22.

With three races remaining and 129 points still available, the championship is very much alive. Las Vegas (Nov 22) is next, with the season finale still to come after that. Every qualifying session, every pit stop, and every overtake from here on carries championship weight.

For fans who love drama, this is what Formula 1 is for.

Character count: 160 ✓

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 10:00 AM ET

Mercedes have sealed the 2026 Constructors' Championship, but the battle for second place is far from over.

Ferrari sit on 510 points. McLaren are on 398. That 112-point gap might look decisive, but with three grands prix still on the schedule — each worth 44 points to a race winner plus fastest lap — McLaren cannot be mathematically eliminated yet.

For the Prancing Horse, the priority is clear: bank the points, avoid retirements, and secure a P2 that would represent a strong season in the face of Mercedes' dominance. For McLaren, it's about fighting to the end and ensuring Norris has every opportunity to close the standings.

The constructors' battle adds another layer of intrigue to what is already a compelling end to the 2026 season.

stories.title: Mercedes' Dominant 2026 — Analyzing How Antonelli and Russell Delivered the Title

x_posts.text:
**Post 1 (Angle: New era)**
Posting window: 10:00 AM ET

Mercedes are 2026 Constructors' Champions. And they did it without Lewis Hamilton for the first time in a decade. Antonelli and Russell. A new era begins. 🥈🥈 #F1 #Mercedes

Character count: 174 ✓

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 10:00 AM ET

A new era of Mercedes dominance is underway — and this time, they did it their way.

For the first time in over a decade, Mercedes won the Constructors' Championship without Lewis Hamilton in the car. Kimi Antonelli — still a teenager when the season began — and George Russell delivered 652 championship points in a campaign that validated the team's bold choice to trust youth alongside experience.

Antonelli, in particular, has been the revelation of the year. His consistency, his racecraft, and his ability to handle the pressure of competing for a world title in his debut season has been exceptional. Russell, a proven race winner, provided the steady anchor that allowed the team to maximize both cars throughout the campaign.

This is what succession planning looks like in Formula 1.

Character count: 110 ✓

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 2:00 PM ET

Eleven days. That's how long F1 fans have to wait before the Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 22.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is one of the most visually spectacular venues on the Formula 1 calendar — and one of the most technically demanding. High-speed straights stretch along the iconic casino corridor, requiring teams to balance low-drag setups with enough downforce to handle the technical sections that separate the best drivers from the field.

For the championship contenders, Las Vegas represents a pivotal moment. Teams will pore over data from previous visits to the circuit, optimizing their car configurations for a race that takes place under the Nevada night sky.

The championship could be settled here. Or it could make the season finale even more dramatic. Either way, Las Vegas is going to deliver.

Posting window: 12:00 PM ET

Kimi Antonelli. Isack Hadjar. The 2026 F1 rookie class has been something else. Podiums, points, and championship battles. The future of F1 is now. #F1 #Rookies

Character count: 162 ✓

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 5:00 PM ET

When the 2026 Formula 1 season began, questions swirled about whether the rookie class could handle the pressure of a full championship campaign.

The answer has been a resounding yes.

Kimi Antonelli arrived at Mercedes as Lewis Hamilton's replacement with the kind of pressure that would buckle most experienced drivers — and responded by putting himself in the championship conversation. The Italian teenager has shown maturity, speed, and racecraft that veterans twice his age struggle to match.

Isack Hadjar, meanwhile, has quietly assembled a solid campaign with Red Bull's affiliate team, earning points and demonstrating that his route to a full Red Bull seat is well and truly established.

The 2026 rookies have not just competed. They have thrived. Formula 1's future is in excellent hands.
